scenario: A buyer has an existing television whose menu reports 4K and 60 Hz, but they have not verified the exact HDMI port, cable, VRR range, or input settings. They are comparing PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and the cheaper Series S after seeing a $52.47 marketplace listing whose title stacks PS5, RDNA 2, 825 GB SSD, and controller claims. Their representative game is Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart, and they also care about multiplatform games. They will buy only if the frozen evidence supports the actual game mode and complete display chain rather than a console maximum, teraflop-style headline, connector label, or promise that an SSD removes every loading screen. If the evidence cannot choose a box on those terms, they will defer and audit their target games and display chain.

rules.complete_console_and_listing_matrix_v1: The frozen marketplace title claims a PS5 disc console with an eight-core Zen CPU, RDNA 2 graphics, 16 GB GDDR6, an 825 GB SSD, one controller, and a skin, but the complete body is $52.47, has no review yet, identifies the brand as Hubxcel, and says the hardware platform is PlayStation 4. It is not a trustworthy verified PS5 offer. The PlayStation 5 page describes a custom SSD, an AMD GPU capable of 4K display at up to 120 frames per second, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, and an HDMI 2.1 output. Those are device capabilities, not a promise that every game combines native 4K, 120 FPS, and ray tracing. The Xbox page says Series X was designed to nominally render 2160p at 60 FPS, while Series S was designed for nominal 1440p at 60 FPS with 4K upscaling and ray tracing; it separately says Series S can go as high as 120 FPS at that resolution and that selected games can output native 4K. The frozen evidence does not establish current street prices or a universal winner for unfrozen games.
rules.game_mode_and_marketing_scope_v1: A console ceiling, a 4K label, and a ray-tracing capability must be checked against a named game and patch mode. The frozen Rift Apart page provides the decisive concrete counterexample: after a launch-day patch it offers a 4K-resolution fidelity mode at 30 FPS and two 60 FPS modes, Performance and Performance Ray-Tracing, at a lower base resolution. Its platform list is PlayStation 5 and Windows, so this one representative game supports a conditional PS5 route, but only for that workload. The ray-tracing concept page says ray-tracing techniques are generally slower and higher fidelity than scanline rendering and historically less suited to real time because every frame has a deadline. The 4K page says 4K is a generic horizontal-resolution family and that 4K and Ultra HD are widely used in marketing. The community thread correctly raises finite compute and quality/performance trade-offs, but its anonymous explanations are not measurements of either console or an authority for other games.
rules.display_hdmi_refresh_chain_v1: FPS is the rate at which a system such as a GPU generates frames, while refresh rate is the rate at which a display shows completed frames. The refresh-rate page says refresh rate is independent from frame rate and determines the highest frame rate that can be displayed. Therefore the scenario's reported 60 Hz television cannot display 120 distinct frames per second in that mode even if the console and game can generate or output them. The HDMI page says source devices read a display's E-EDID to learn which audio and video formats it accepts, reinforcing that the sink matters. The VRR page says a supporting display has a specific VRR range and matches its refresh to the incoming frame rate within that range. A console's HDMI 2.1 output or VRR support does not prove that the intended television port, cable, input setting, and supported range complete the chain. Preflight the exact port, cable, TV input mode, accepted 3840 by 2160 refresh modes, HDR mode, and VRR range, then confirm the console's detected-output screen and the chosen game's mode.
rules.storage_and_loading_scope_v1: An SSD is technically meaningful but does not erase software and workload boundaries. The generic SSD page says SSDs have no moving parts and provide faster data access and reduced latency relative to hard disks. The PS5 page says reducing loading time was an important design goal. The Xbox page says both models have SSDs to reduce loading times. Rift Apart ties its custom SSD and greater processing power to more objects and effects and says its design aims to significantly reduce loading times when jumping between worlds. None of these exact statements says every loading screen in every game is eliminated, and no frozen page measures the buyer's complete game library. Audit per-game load behavior, installation location, patch, and transitions rather than converting an SSD label into a universal zero-load claim.
rules.evidence_bounded_console_decision_v1: Do not purchase the $52.47 marketplace listing from its headline, and do not choose a console from 4K120, ray tracing, teraflops, SSD, or HDMI 2.1 stickers alone. On the one frozen game-specific workload, PlayStation 5 is the only conditionally supported console route because Rift Apart is listed for PS5 and provides explicit 4K/30 and lower-base-resolution/60 modes, including Performance Ray-Tracing. That does not prove simultaneous native 4K, 120 FPS, and ray tracing, nor does the scenario's 60 Hz display expose a 120 FPS benefit. If Rift Apart is truly the buyer's priority, choose a verified real PS5 listing only after the exact game mode and display-chain preflight. If the buyer instead needs a cross-platform or Xbox title comparison, defer: the frozen corpus does not contain matched game-mode measurements, current prices, or library preferences that justify a PS5-versus-Series-X winner. Series S must be described as nominal 1440p/60 with 4K upscaling and selected exceptions, not as a universal native-4K substitute.
